title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC0RC_0LD1LC_1RE1LB_1RF---_1LE1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC0RC_0LD1LC_1RE1LB_1RF---_1LE1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, partly decoded. At the left end of the tape the machine runs a doubling chain: a block of x ones becomes 2x+12 ones each time an item 1^7 0 follows it, by a transfer that moves the ones two at a time into copies of 10 (both proved in Lean). The chains make the giant blocks of ones and take nearly all the running time. What the sweeps do to the rest of the word, and so how long each chain gets, is not decoded; no halt in 7.3·1012 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,047 cells have been visited and 28,773 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three giant blocks of ones, to 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: Run from blank tape, the tape at a full sweep is a word over the tokens 1 and a = 10. Three times so far one token run dominates: a block of 102 ones at step 11,869 (tape 144 cells), 1,730 ones at step 3,472,160 (1,918 cells) and 49,142 ones at step 2,820,772,373 (52,484 cells). Each comes after a long stretch with no full sweep, and is followed by sweeps that rewrite it as a^k and then into periodic words ((1^2 a)^k, (1^4 a^2)^k, (1^6 a)^k, …). No halt.

claims.title: The transfer at the left end
claims.text: Write G for the left end of the tape 0^inf 1 1 1 0 1 0 1 1 0 with the head in C on a 0. Then G (10)^(2j+1) 1^3 R becomes G (10)^(2j+3) 1 R in 28j+64 steps, for every j and every tape R to the right: two ones become two more copies of 10, and the tape grows by two cells on the left. Repeated n times it costs n(28j+14n+50) steps.

claims.title: The doubling chain
claims.text: G 10 1^x (10)^3 1^5 0 1^7 0 R with x = 2n+2 becomes G 10 1^(2x+12) (10)^3 1^5 0 R: the transfer empties the block of ones, one more pass turns the 2n+1 copies of 10 into 4n+16 ones, and the item 1^7 0 is used up. With c items in a row the block grows to 2c(x+12)−12 ones.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.3·10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: A C simulator that applies the transfer in closed form and steps the machine cell by cell otherwise reaches step 7,298,767,517,608 (tape 5,146,290 cells) without a halt. Its left-end configurations are checked against the plain machine for the first 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps (122 configurations, all on the plain run). Chains seen: blocks of 181, 373, …, 24,565 ones (ending at step 2.8·10<sup>9</sup>), then up to 786,429 ones (step 2.9·10<sup>12</sup>) and 786,421 ones (step 5.8·10<sup>12</sup>); every long chain so far passes through 3,061, 6,133, 12,277 ones.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: The chain at the left end is understood, but its length is set by how many items 1^7 0 stand in a row after the block, and these are made by the sweeps over the rest of the word, which act like a transducer that has not been decoded. Halting needs the head in D on a 0 followed by 1 or by 0 0; whether the word can ever present that is not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Every sweep rewrites the tape, a word over 1 and 10. At the left end a block of ones doubles again and again, once for each item 1^7 0 that follows it; that part is proved. What the sweeps do to the rest of the word is not decoded.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,047 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The largest block of ones seen, at step 2.8·10<sup>9</sup>.

sections.heading: A word rewritten at every sweep
html: The head sweeps the whole tape, and at each end the tape reads as a word over two tokens, a single 1 and a = 10, written here run-length coded. Early on the word looks irregular and changes at every sweep:

steptape

3401^8 a^6 1^11
3801^2 a^4 1^12 a^5
430a^2 1^2 a 1^2 a^7 1^2 a 1^2 a 1^3
Then come long stretches in which the head never reaches both ends, and after them one token run fills most of the tape:

The following sweeps rewrite it in a regular way: 1^49144 becomes a^24572, then (1^2 a)^k, (1^4 a^2)^k, (1^6 a)^k, (1^2 a^3)^k and so on, as if each sweep were a fixed transducer on the word. The ratios between the giant blocks, 17 and 28, and the times, 290 and 810, say that the next one is far away (a guess from the growth of these ratios: 1012 to 1013 steps).

sections.heading: The transfer and the doubling chain
html: The long stretches without a full sweep are spent at the left end of the tape. Write G for 0^inf 1 1 1 0 1 0 1 1 0 with the head in state C on a 0.

Transfer. G (10)^(2j+1) 1^3 R becomes G (10)^(2j+3) 1 R in 28j+64 steps: the head turns the copies of 10 into ones on its way right, takes two ones off the block, comes back writing copies of 10, and does this twice; the tape grows by two cells on the left. A block of m ones is emptied in about m/2 transfers and 3.5·m2 steps.

Doubling. When two ones are left and the word (10)^3 1^5 0 1^7 0 follows, one more pass turns the 2j+1 copies of 10 into 4j+16 ones and uses up the item 1^7 0. Together: a block of x ones becomes 2x+12 ones.

(The count includes the first one of the following (10)^3: 181 = 180 + 1, and 372 = 2·180 + 12.) Both rules are proved in Lean for every j and every tape to the right. A chain goes on as long as items 1^7 0 follow; later chains reach 786,429 ones. Which items the sweeps leave there is the part that is not decoded.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.392). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,047 cells (25,437 left of the start, 289 right), with a density of 1s of 0.777.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Finding the transducer
html: To get further one would write the effect of a full sweep on the token word as rules (symtm can prove each once found), find what invariant the word keeps between giant blocks, and so reduce the run to a map on a few numbers. None of that has been done.

summary: Sweeps rewrite a word over 1 and 10. At the left end a doubling chain (x ones -> 2x+12 per item 1^7 0, proved in Lean) makes giant blocks of ones; the rest of the word is not decoded. No halt in 7.3e12 steps.
family: sweeping transducer on a block word; doubling chain at the left end proved, the rest undecoded
